text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SiennaBank-prod (VPC) ap-southeast1 dedicated pool - p99 latency > 8s for 7m. Impact: customer-visible SLO breach. Paging oncall-sre. Links: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1719854321 :rotating_light:

Alex L: @oncall-sre - I’m in. grabbing traces now. Do we have a tenant-level hotspot or whole pool?

oncall-sre: saw the alert, joining. Initial check: control plane shows high queue depth on pool:sienna-apse1-dedicated-01. Metrics: CPU GPU utilization normal, but queue_time and scheduling latency spike.

Sara K: I’m pulling flamegraphs and kv cache hit rates. early signal: KV cache miss rate for SiennaBank traffic up ~40% vs baseline. Could be cache invalidation or a topology mismatch.

Mike R: Replaying recent deploys - no deploys in last 3h. Autoscaler shows failed scale-out attempts at 12:34 UTC (rate limit from infra-api). Could be throttling on node provisioning.

Jen P: @Alex L can you run a targeted tail of the inference runtime logs for tenant=sienna-bank?

Alex L: running now. logs show repeated grpc connection resets to backend worker 10.4.23.7 and then backpressure backoff. snippet: ```
E030 12:33:57.123 worker_handler.cpp:211] grpc::StatusCode::UNAVAILABLE: connection reset by peer
W030 12:34:01.456 scheduler.cpp:84] queue_size=312 scheduling_delay_ms=1280
```

Arjun S: sounds like transient worker OOM or driver crash. infra logs? @InfraBot pull kernel OOMs for that node.

InfraBot: OOM check for 10.4.23.7: no kernel OOMs. Docker exited containers: runtime exited due to SIGABRT at 12:33:56. System level CPU/RAM OK. GPU watchdog events at 12:33:55 on gpu0: stall_detected.

oncall-sre: GPU stall -> worker restarted and then cluster scheduler pushed more requests to remaining workers -> queue amplification -> p99 spike. Immediate mitigations: 1) isolate SiennaBank traffic to fallback routing; 2) drain and reprovision affected node(s); 3) temporarily scale dedicated pool by +2 nodes from spare capacity pool.

Sara K: For fallback, we can route tenant to a lighter model variant (quantized) in ap-southeast1 while we fix the pool. That reduces latency and GPU pressure. I can update routing policy.

Mike R: I’ll open a capacity request. CLI: ```redwood infra allocate --pool spare-apse1 --count 2 --labels temp-for-sienna``` executing now. If provision fails, we fallback to cross-region routing to ap-southeast2 (latency penalty, but keeps SLO).

Alex L: Applying a canary routing override now for tenant:sienna-bank -> model:rw-ggml-q4_1-128 (quantized). Command: ```
redwood route override set --tenant sienna-bank --pool ap-southeast1 --model rw-ggml-q4_1-128 --ttl 15m --reason "incident mitigation"
```

IncidentBot: NOTE: routing override applied by Alex L at 12:38 UTC.

Maya (CS): I’ve alerted SiennaBank points-of-contact: "We are seeing elevated latency, mitigation in progress, may route some traffic to a temporary model to restore performance. We will update within 30 mins." Customer asked for ETA.

Jen P: Draining node 10.4.23.7 now. Command: ```kubectl cordon node-10-4-23-7 && kubectl drain node-10-4-23-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``` Watching for graceful session handoff.

InfraBot: Node cordoned and drain started. Drained pods: 18. Eviction took ~45s each; healthchecks show handoffs completed. Node reprovision job queued.

Mike R: Allocation returned success - 2 nodes provisioned from spare pool (node-10.4.24.10, node-10.4.24.11). Added to pool. Autoscaler reports new capacity ready at 12:46 UTC.

Sara K: post-routing p99 down from 8.5s -> 450ms for tenant traffic. KV-cache warmup in progress; hit-rate climbing back to baseline.

Alex L: rolling restart of worker binary on drained node confirmed cause: GPU watchdog flagged a busy loop triggered by unexpected nvml call retry in runtime v1.3.2. Hotfix plan: patch runtime with nvml retry backoff (v1.3.3) and rollout to pool.

Arjun S: Recommend constrained rollout: apply to 10% of nodes, monitor p99 and error-rate for 10m, then continue. I’ll create rollout job. Command: ```
redwood deploy runtime --version v1.3.3 --scope pool:sienna-apse1 --parallel 2 --health-check 10m
```

oncall-sre: handoff to day oncall in 18m. Action items before handoff: 1) Confirm runtime rollout started and healthy. 2) Keep routing override active until KV hit-rate >= 85% for 15m. 3) Customer comms update in 20m. 4) Postmortem owner assigned.

Maya (CS): I’ll draft the 20m status update to customer.

Alex L: Patch rollout started at 12:52 UTC, first batch healthy after 6m. No regressions so far.

Jen P: Node reprovision finished, nodes stabilized. Drained node will be inspected offline.

IncidentBot: RESOLVED: p99 latency for SiennaBank back within SLO < 1s at 12:58 UTC. Monitoring will remain elevated for 1h. Postmortem owner: Arjun S. Tags: customer-impact, dedicated-pool, gpu-watchdog. :white_check_mark:

Arjun S: Assigning postmortem. I’ll collect timeline, logs, and the rollout notes. Tentative RCA: GPU watchdog-triggered worker crash exacerbated by dense fanout from dedicated pool; mitigation included routing to quantized model, adding capacity, and runtime hotfix.

Sara K: Captured some follow-ups: improve GPU watchdog telemetry (more granular reasons), add autoscaler retry backoff, add tenant-priority throttles to avoid single-tenant amplification.

Mike R: I’ll submit a capacity incident runbook change to ensure we have a faster spare-node allocation path for dedicated pools.

oncall-sre: Handoff complete to day-oncall. Leaving notes in incident doc and PagerDuty. Great job team. :tada:
